code: bp_conservative <- regsen_bounds(form, bfg2020, compare = w1,                                   cbar = 1) bp_relaxed <- regsen_bounds(form, bfg2020, compare = w1,                              cbar = 1,                              rybar_expr = function(rx) rx) # `digits` is the precision the paper actually prints each value to, given # explicitly rather than inferred. Deriving it from format() is wrong: # format() pads a vector to a common width, so format(c(0.804, 0.96)) is # c("0.804", "0.960") and 0.96 would be held to a precision it was never # printed at. compare_published <- function(quantity, published, computed, digits) {     out <- data.frame(         quantity  = quantity,         published = published,         computed  = round(computed, 4),         stringsAsFactors = FALSE     )     out$difference <- round(out$computed - out$published, 4)     out$agrees <- abs(out$difference) <= 0.5 * 10^(-digits)     out }  cmp <- compare_published(     quantity  = c("rxbar^bp at cbar = 1",                   "r^bp at cbar = 1, rybar = rxbar"),     published = c(0.804, 0.96),     digits    = c(3, 2),          # as printed in the paper     computed  = c(bp_conservative$breakdown, bp_relaxed$breakdown) ) knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Breakdown points: this package vs DMP (2026).")

text: Regression sensitivity analysis omitted-variable bias R. Implements identified-set breakdown-point analyses described : Diegert, Masten Poirier (2026) — bounds long-regression coefficient relaxations -omitted-variables assumption, indexed rxbar / rybar / cbar. Oster (2019) — identified set (delta, R²(long)) associated breakdown point. Masten Poirier (2026) — extension maximum omitted-variable-bias constraint. arXiv working papers still revised periodically; citations package track year latest arXiv revision. package provides formula + data.frame API, ggplot2-based plotting, percentile/cluster bootstrap breakdown point.
